newsitem.title: MEXICO: GF Bancomer Q1 1997 net 349 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: GF Bancomer Q1 1997 net 349 mln pesos.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Bancomer on Wednesday reported a profit of 349 million pesos in the first quarter of 1997, with its banking unit Bancomer showing a gain of 305 million pesos.

The profits, reported under new U.S. GAAP accounting rules, compared with losses in Q1 1996 under the old accounting system of 1.865 billion pesos at the group level, and 1.939 billion pesos in the banking unit.
Bancomer's capitalization ratio at the end of the quarter was 14.36 percent, compared with 12.18 percent at the end of 1996. Its provisions against past-due loans were 57.5 percent.
GFB issued the following table of its results:

Bancomer 305 million 897 million -1.939 bln

Bancomer Forex -5 million 4 million 9 million

Bancomer Warehousing 0 10 million 3 million
Family Credit -3 million 0 n.a
It said it has decided how to raise 80 percent of the capital that it had pledged to accumulate this year in exchange for its sale of past-due loans to the government in 1996 and 1997.

The funds would come from the agreed sale of some assets of Bancomer Warehousing (Almacenadora Bancomer) to the warehousing firm Accelsa, a deal it said it hoped to complete in the second quarter. The remaining Almacenadora assets would be merged with Bancomer and both operations would provide 250 million pesos of capital, it said.
Also, during the second quarter Bancomer brokerage would pay a dividend of some 150 million pesos to Bancomer.
The group gave the following additional breakdown of its results:
-- Operating profit: 3.519 billion pesos, up 443 million from Q4 1996, mainly because of trading income.

-- Financial revenues: 9.136 billion pesos, down 9.6 percent from the previous quarter. It said the decline was offset by a monetary gain of 278 million pesos, which raised its net financial margin to 5.8 percent from 5.6 percent in Q4 1996.
-- Asset quality: Net past-due loans were 9.22 percent, and gross past-dues, not including loans sold to Bank Insurance Fund Fobaproa, were 19.2 percent of total loans.
-- Reserves against past-due loans: It created 1.058 billion pesos of reserves in the quarter.
Bancomer also opened 60 new branches during the quarter, giving it 1,323 outlets as of March 31.
